sections.h2: Which offices handle a Mesquite tax bill?
sections.html:
Part of Mesquite sits in Dallas County and part in Kaufman County, which means an owner should check the county before calling anyone. The county decides who values the house and who takes the check. The city's tax page prints a separate table of rates for each side.

Austin collects nothing on real estate. A county appraisal district puts a value on the house each January 1, and then five local bodies, from the city to Parkland Hospital, apply their own rates to it.

  • Dallas County parcels: Dallas Central Appraisal District, 214-631-0520, for value and exemptions; the Dallas County tax office, 214-653-7811, for city and Mesquite ISD bills.
  • Kaufman County parcels: Kaufman Central Appraisal District in the town of Kaufman, 972-932-6081.
  • Past-due accounts: the city page lists Grimes & Linebarger, LLP at 120 West Main, Suite 201 in Mesquite, 469-942-2011.

Exemption forms are the one errand the city's tax office cannot run for you, according to its own page.

sections.h2: What 2025 rates apply to a Mesquite house?
sections.html:
The city's 2025 rate is $0.7046920 per $100 of assessed value, with the rest of the bill set by the county line. Mesquite ISD, Dallas College and Parkland Hospital charge the same on either side of that line.

Mesquite's page says recent state-level changes have noticeably lowered resident bills, pointing to the larger homestead exemption and the extra help for owners who are over 65 or disabled, both of which cut school taxes. It links to estimating tools for each county, so you can test your own parcel instead of guessing at a total.

The page also records a 2024 city rate of 0.69000 and a 2024 school rate of 1.09920. A footnote cautions that other taxing units may be added to the totals, so look up your own parcel at the appraisal district before quoting a figure.

sections.h2: What happens after January 31 in Mesquite?
sections.html:
Statements are mailed in October and can be paid on arrival. Dallas County treats an account as late once January 31 has gone by, and it reads the postmark on a mailed check. Not receiving the statement does not excuse the tax or the late charges.

The Comptroller says the first day of February brings a penalty of 6 percent plus interest of 1 percent. Interest keeps adding a point a month with no stopping point, and the penalty rises a point a month until it tops out at 12 percent in July.

  • Dallas County hands non-business accounts to its collection attorney on July 1, and the attorney's fee can reach 20 percent.
  • To ask for a waiver of the charges, send the request in writing before day 181 of delinquency and settle the tax within 21 days of finding out it was late.
  • Some collectors write instalment agreements running as long as 36 months, and a residence homestead is the only case where one must be offered.
  • Seniors and disabled owners may split the bill into four payments.

sections.h2: How can a Mesquite owner shrink the bill?
sections.html:
Start with age. The city page lists a $65,000 exemption for homeowners over 65 and a $15,000 exemption for disabled persons, and a person gets one or the other. Either one also brings a ceiling: the city and school taxes stay at what you paid in the first qualifying year until you build onto the house or move.

School taxes have a state-set break of their own, $140,000 off a residence homestead and $60,000 more for older or disabled owners.

  • Disabled veterans exempt $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating, rising to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent, and a 100 percent rating can wipe out the homestead's taxable value.
  • A homestead's appraised value is capped at a 10 percent yearly rise, beginning the year after the first exemption.
  • Heirs whose names are not on the recorded deed send the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: When must a Mesquite owner file a value protest?
sections.html:
File the written protest with the Appraisal Review Board by May 15, or 30 days after delivery of the notice when that is later. Homestead notices start going out around April 1, and notices for other property follow near May 1.

Dallas County's tax office refers all protest questions to the appraisal districts, so a Dallas County parcel is disputed at Dallas Central Appraisal District and a Kaufman County parcel at Kaufman Central Appraisal District. Owners who lose at the board have further routes: district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values above $1,000,000. Pay the portion nobody disputes before the cutoff, or the appeal will not protect you from penalties.

sections.h2: How big is Mesquite, according to the Census?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts describes a city whose headcount has barely moved since 2020:

  • Population: 150,693 in the July 2025 estimate, 150,108 in the 2020 census, 139,824 in 2010.
  • Size: 48.48 square miles of land, which held 3,096.1 people a mile in 2020.
  • Ownership: 62.8 percent of homes are lived in by their owners (2020-2024 survey), and the midpoint value is $245,700.
  • Money: gross rent at the midpoint is $1,513 and household income at the midpoint is $72,537.
  • Households: 50,171, averaging 2.96 people.
  • Commute: 32.1 minutes on average.
  • Age: 11.3 percent of residents are 65 or older, the people eligible for the city's larger exemption.

sections.h2: What should a Mesquite seller check before closing?
sections.html:
The tax lien keys off who owns the house on January 1. Whoever holds title that day owes the whole year, even when the sale closes in March. Ask the title company how the bill will be divided with the buyer, and read the payoff lines of its commitment.

A buyer closing after the new year may apply for the homestead exemption immediately if the seller never had it. Sellers should confirm what is owed with the Dallas County Tax Office, or the Kaufman County tax office for a Kaufman parcel.

When the account has already gone to the collection attorney, ask for a written payoff itemizing penalty, interest and court costs. The title company needs that figure to clear the lien when the sale funds.

Before you list, gather the latest statement from each taxing unit, your homestead exemption confirmation if you have one, and any protest paperwork from the spring. Tell the title company if a protest is still open, since a successful one changes the tax figure that the closing statement is built around, and note the hearing date for the buyer.

faqs.q: Why does the Kaufman County side of Mesquite show a higher total rate?
faqs.a: Only the county line changes. The city's table shows 0.2155000 for Dallas County and 0.4275260 for Kaufman County, which produces printed totals of 2.3456670 and 2.5576930.

faqs.q: Until what date can Mesquite taxes be paid without charges?
faqs.a: January 31, per Dallas County. Charges begin February 1 and grow each month into July.

faqs.q: How much does Mesquite exempt for homeowners over 65?
faqs.a: $65,000 for owners over 65 and $15,000 for disabled persons, per the city, and one person gets only one of the two. Mesquite ISD applies its own state-mandated amounts.

faqs.q: Where do I pick up a homestead exemption form for a house in Mesquite?
faqs.a: Call the appraisal district for your county, Dallas Central at 214-631-0520 or Kaufman Central at 972-932-6081. The city's tax office does not issue them.

faqs.q: Can a Mesquite house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company gets a payoff from the collection attorney and pays it at closing, since the lien follows the property until then.
